scope: Combined final Phase 2.11 + Phase 3 acceptance; MVP through Outbox, native local signing, NIP-46 on both hosts and Android NIP-55.
excluded: Value transfers, zaps, Value Lab and CAP-13 (Phase 4)

source.description: Original Phase 2.11 matrix bytes are privately preserved; this digest identifies the inherited snapshot without requiring a private path.

phase3RequirementStatusSource.description: Source requirements ledger snapshot, privately preserved.

policy: status and inheritedStatus preserve historical coverage. campaignStatus alone records the combined final campaign; every applicable platform starts not-run, including rows with historical passes. No current campaign pass is inferred.
Inherited platform status values are exact historical snapshots, not validation against the current code candidate. Keep earlier failures and narrower successes separately.
Run case steps on each listed platform. Each requirement also requires its row-specific requiredEvidence; passing a shared case does not automatically pass every mapped row.

During development use simulator/emulator checks where faithful; name the missing capability before a targeted physical check. Final sign-off needs ordinary standalone Android+iOS journeys on final artifact hashes.
Run embedded and verified-published variants for all applicable capability groups. Every signing route runs with local and NIP-46 on both platforms and NIP-55 on Android.
No fallback, automatic resend, deadline reset or unsupported-operation authority may be inferred. Unknown remains unknown until independently reconciled.
Normal final quality requires React Doctor and aislop both 100/100; historical exception wording is retained only as history and does not waive the current gate.
No new final pass follows from this planning artifact. Preserve detailed original evidence and limitations before retiring any legacy matrix.

requiredFields: UTC start/end and monotonic clock domain for deadline assertions
source tree digest plus commit and dirty state
Android/iOS platform, OS and runtime version using neutral target aliases
method and exact public account alias
limitations, unresolved side effects and cleanup result
evidenceRecord.privacy: Public evidence uses portable repository-relative paths and retired disposable public test data. Never commit device IDs, private vault references, credentials, callback tokens, raw nsec, raw operational logs or personal paths. Retain sensitive originals outside the public artifact; publish only reviewed summaries/digests.

testCases.title: Header, identity and theme
steps: Cold-launch and inspect the expanded shelf header; open UX Lab and another napplet to inspect the compact focused header. Exercise the All napplets spark, focused-title menu and identity Settings control; copy the full public npub from Settings.
Use two disposable accounts with valid, missing and broken profile images; switch and cold-launch each. Change system light/dark appearance.
expected: Expanded shelf header uses a 32-point noninteractive logo and short selected npub. The focused header uses a 24-point All napplets spark in a 44-point control, plain centered title opening the menu, and avatar Settings with the full npub accessibility label. Settings/copy/focused title agree with the selected account/view. Reconcile this current source-backed compact profile with the preserved historical UX-01 wording before a final campaign pass.
A valid profile image appears; otherwise the same account gets the same local fallback, with no stale previous-account image. Theme remains readable.
evidence: Screenshots and accessibility tree for each profile state; exact public npub comparison; copy result; before/after restart.

testCases.title: Workspace navigation and retained views
steps: Open three UX/State Lab instances in order. Enter distinct unsent text/counter values and vertical/horizontal scroll markers. Navigate previous/next with real handle drags and tap each handle for overview.
Release a short drag early; drag at both ends; interact with near-edge guest controls. Select each overview card and open a fourth view.
Save State Lab data; close/reopen it. Close all views; cold-launch. Repeat cold launch with multiple saved views and a selected last view.
expected: Opening order is stable; new views append; focus never reorders. No wrap, false navigation or lost live text/scroll position. Drag follows input and short cancellation returns.
Two-column overview has correct transition geometry and selected view. Close keeps saved data, leaves overview, and last close yields accessible Open napplet/settings.
Restart preserves deliberate empty state or order, verified version and last selected view; other views reload lazily. Unsaved process-death recovery is not required.
evidence: Actual input/transition recording; accessibility order and visible scroll markers; saved-value readback; pre/post cold-launch snapshots.

testCases.title: Clean, dirty and unknown close
steps: Use the selected dirty-state contract to prepare clean, dirty and unknown sessions; arm a pending approval in each. Swipe its overview card upward.
Choose default Keep open, then repeat and choose Close anyway. Send a late callback and reopen the napplet.
expected: Clean closes directly; dirty/unknown warn with Keep open as default. Cancellation preserves the session; accepted close tears it down.
Old pending/approved authority is revoked and cannot be replayed after reopen; new work requires a fresh request/review.
evidence: Trusted warning screenshots; exact session IDs represented by neutral aliases; native cancellation/sign counters and independent network counts.

testCases.title: Input, accessibility and motion
steps: With the OS keyboard open, edit long JSON and navigate focused view, overview, Settings, review and results using Android Back or iOS dismiss/navigation.
Enable large text, TalkBack/VoiceOver and OS reduced motion. Traverse controls, reject and approve distinct requests, and inspect long event/list/destination/result data.
expected: Controls stay reachable and readable without hidden next actions; focus returns sensibly; Android Back and iOS gestures obey review/queue policy.

Accessible names identify action/account/requester; keyboard and edge gestures do not conflict. Reduced motion changes transitions without breaking navigation. Primary/list receipts and unknown outcomes stay distinguishable.
evidence: OS setting witness; actual key/gesture and focus recording; screen-reader traversal; full review and receipt captures with safe public fixtures.

testCases.title: Native identity creation, import and storage
steps: On a fresh disposable app profile, cold-launch and independently compare the derived public npub; repeat process death/reboot and restore.
Import valid nsec through native trusted Settings; test cancel, malformed/out-of-range input and authentication denial. Retain and select the previous account; cold-launch both.
Inject missing/corrupt/tampered storage, unavailable protection and read/write failures using the owning test harness. Inspect native/JS/guest surfaces, backup configuration and sanitized artifacts.

On physical targets, lock/background during native vault, import and backup access; test unavailable protected data, screenshot/recording and OS task-preview capture on protected surfaces without retaining any raw secret.

Exercise actual supported OS backup and device-transfer transport with disposable profiles; inspect what is restored/copied and compare native secret/identity protection. Configuration exclusion alone is insufficient.
expected: Exactly one local account is created on first launch without requiring an external signer. The same account survives restart; a failed read never silently creates a replacement.
Secrets are created/imported/read/signed only in native ownership; encrypted persistence and native protection fail closed; import cancellation preserves state.
No raw secret crosses Expo/React/guest storage or public logs/artifacts; automatic backup exclusion and at-rest integrity are verified. Simulator storage doubles do not establish physical protection.

Native authentication, protected-data availability and capture policy match the selected platform design; denied/late access cannot expose secrets or revive a cancelled owner. Record each demonstrated protection and limitation separately.
Real backup/device-transfer behavior honors the selected exclusion/protection design; failures never create or expose a replacement identity.
evidence: Public identity equality; owning native failure results; encrypted-record/config inspection; bridge-surface review; sanitized absence checks and physical protection evidence.
Physical lock/authentication/capture observations with no secret-bearing image or raw key in the evidence.
Actual backup/transfer transport observations, restored-record/protection checks and sanitized guest/shared/React persistence, heap, log/crash failure-surface inspection.

testCases.title: Backup and account deletion
steps: Explain manual nsec backup, then test native device authentication success/cancel/unavailable/late completion; compare reimported public identity without recording the secret.

Try deleting the only account. Add another account, then test delete cancel, auth failure and success; cold-launch the survivor. Keep a surviving napplet with an unsaved live draft during successful deletion and verify its session/draft continues before testing cold survivor persistence.
expected: Backup reveals only after valid current native authentication; cancellation/expiry/failure exports nothing and cannot extend the absolute deadline.

Last-account deletion is unavailable; confirmed authenticated deletion removes only the intended encrypted record and revokes its sessions. Surviving account remains usable. Successful deletion preserves the survivor's currently loaded session and live draft; cold identity continuity alone does not prove that behavior.
evidence: Native authentication/expiry result and zero-export counter; public reimport comparison; encrypted-record presence/absence; survivor restart. Physical authentication is required.

testCases.title: Account and publisher isolation
steps: With three sessions and pending approval/upload/stream/channel work, begin an account switch and cancel it. Verify all original registrations and values still work.
Confirm the switch. Exercise late callbacks and replay from the old identity, then switch back and cold-launch.
Write distinct State Lab values under account A/B, publisher A/B and stable app ID A/B. Update the same verified app version; also try a publisher collision.
Exercise State storage quota/type errors and forged caller-supplied namespaces, with valid same-scope positive controls before and after denial.
expected: Cancelled switch preserves original sessions, configuration and routing. Confirmed switch warns once, revokes old work and restarts all sessions under one selected account.
No old request/result crosses accounts. Storage is scoped by selected account + verified publisher + stable app identity; valid same-app updates retain data; other scopes cannot read it.
Quota/type/namespace faults return canonical errors without cross-scope reads, writes, partial corruption or guest-selected namespaces.
evidence: Scope/value cross-product; cancelled/confirmed switch input; stale reply/sign/send counters; exact restored data and public account snapshots.

testCases.title: Trusted review and serialized queue
steps: Submit one note and another supported kind, then three queued requests across focused/unfocused sessions. Inspect full canonical event, requester/publisher/version, account and selected signer before Approve once or Reject.
Dismiss/back/swipe the current review. Focus another view and let its delayed request arrive; return and explicitly resume the queue.
Mutate, reorder, duplicate and replay request/session/version/account payloads before and after review.

For verified-published relay publication, leave review pending beyond 30 seconds but within the native approval deadline, then resolve it once. Require the original SDK request/result and no premature client failure or retransmission; the 660-second response budget must not extend native approval authority.
expected: Every supported publication uses one exact native-owned, one-use approval; no Approve all or silent route. Dismiss rejects current and pauses the remainder.
Unfocused requests wait without stealing focus; overview indicates pending work. Only explicit resume proceeds.
Approved bytes/account/source/generation/version remain immutable across asynchronous signing. Forged or stale inputs cannot sign.
evidence: Complete native review; queue order/focus recording; independent canonical event ID and Schnorr verification; native one-use/sign counters.

testCases.title: Publication outcomes and authority races
steps: Approve, reject, cancel and expire a request before signing; then interrupt at pending, native signing, dispatch, sent-awaiting-reply and receipt boundaries.
At each boundary background/lock/return, close/switch/update the view, change account/method/relay, revoke/disconnect and kill/restart the process. Deliver late/duplicate replies.
Retry only by explicit fresh request/review after reconciling any possible prior side effect.
expected: Pre-dispatch denial produces zero signing/emission when independently measured. Old authority never revives after lifecycle changes.
Possible dispatch/signing with no verified final outcome stays uncertain; cancellation is not proof of no effect. No automatic retry, local fallback, reapproval reuse or deadline reset occurs.
evidence: Native operation/epoch/signature/dispatch counters; controlled receiver frames and event validation; independent receipts/readback; original failure and uncertainty records.
variants: Run local and NIP-46 on Android+iOS; run NIP-55 on Android. Repeat publication, Outbox and Blossom route boundaries.

testCases.title: Verified loading, access and update
steps: Open exact signed artifacts from two controlled publishers through ordinary Settings. Review publisher, signed event/version and requested/available capabilities; decline, then accept fresh consent.
Try malformed identifiers, wrong kind/publisher, bad signature/hash, missing/oversized resources and unsupported or ungranted operations; observe guest execution markers.
Offer valid v2 and invalid/rollback updates while v1 has unsaved data and pending work. Decline, then accept explicit verified update; cold-launch and revoke access.
expected: Only verified exact bytes execute after explicit access review. Unsupported groups are truthfully reported under the selected tolerant-admission policy and receive no native authority.

No unrelated fallback code or invented wire field is used. Decline preserves v1/data; accepted update pins v2, follows dirty-state policy and revokes old authority; cold launch restores the exact pinned version.
evidence: Publisher/event/hash/fixture parity; first-open/update/revoke input and code marker; original SDK operation errors; pinned version after restart.

testCases.title: Relay settings, queries and streams
steps: Inspect separate startup Network and Lookup lists. Add/edit/remove/restore defaults explicitly; reject invalid URLs and cold-launch the saved selection.
Query controlled signed event sets and empty EOSE. Exercise bounded filters/destinations/results, denial, required authentication, reject/offline/timeout and revoked owner.

Open/close caller-owned streams. Send duplicates/flood, disconnect/reconnect, background/return; switch/close/update/account-change while callbacks are pending. Test fresh/stale/corrupt/cross-account cache and foreground refresh.
expected: Roles remain distinct; defaults seed only first use and restore only by explicit action. Empty success differs from incomplete/failure.
Selected authentication obeys the pinned contract and explicit approval policy. Streams respect bounds and selected reconnect policy; close/revocation prevents stale delivery.
Cache freshness and incomplete results remain truthful across cold restart/account changes; public follows never silently change routing.
evidence: Exact role/destination list; independent relay frames/EOSE/event verification; bounded queue counters; close and restart snapshots; no stale callback evidence.

testCases.title: Resource bytes and private handles
steps: Request each selected resource scheme with known image/audio/video bytes; compare full returned bytes/hash and actual native rendering/playback.
Try forbidden destinations/redirects, MIME mismatch, oversize/truncated data, cancellation, cache reuse and stale/cross-session handles; close/update/change account and terminate the content process.
expected: Only selected bounded destinations/content types return verified complete bytes. Cancelled/revoked resources stop; private handles cannot outlive or cross their owning session/account.
Navigation/renderer/resource failure tears down authority and subscriptions; reload never inherits privilege.
evidence: Independent served-byte/hash ledger; native rendering/playback; denied destination receiver counts; handle lifetime and cleanup observations.

testCases.title: Upload preparation, approval and recovery
steps: Pick prepared photos and unchanged attachments. Cancel/revoke the picker recipient; then inspect exact preview, MIME, size, prepared bytes/hash, destination and requester before file approval and native signing consent.
Perform one selected Blossom upload with local and NIP-46 signing; on Android repeat with NIP-55. Independently verify authorization event, exact uploaded bytes and SDK receipt.

Exercise denial, expired grants, changed bytes/destination, bounded queues, partial transfer, disconnect/restart and uncertain server outcome. Reconcile by selected recovery path before explicit retry.
expected: Native preparation precedes guest handoff; approval and exact-file PUT permit bind the actual prepared/original hash, account/source/version and destination. No guest MIME/name can choose sanitation policy.
No signing capture/claim precedes file approval; late/cancelled authority cannot PUT. Possible sent bytes remain uncertain across restart without duplicate resend.
Native server confirmation, provider readback and durable storage/enforcement are separately evidenced.
evidence: Picker/preview/input record; native file/sign/PUT counters; independent server authorization and payload hash; SDK result; durable uncertainty record/restart reconciliation.

testCases.title: Public identity reads
steps: Read selected profile, relays, follows, mutes, global lists and accepted badges through genuine State/Feed SDK calls using two accounts and known signed records.
Exercise missing/invalid/stale/corrupt records, freshness/refresh, persisted grants/revoke, delayed delivery, publisher collision and cold restart.
expected: Only validated selected public data is returned with canonical missing/error forms and truthful freshness. Grants/results remain source/account scoped; revocation drops queued results.
Separate list review obeys selected policy; reading follows does not alter relay routing.
evidence: Independent signed source records; typed SDK outputs; selected grant review; cross-account/publisher negative controls and restart.

testCases.title: External links
steps: Deliberately open each selected external-link scheme through Resource Lab and native review/control.
Try forbidden schemes/embedded credentials, automatic/flood requests, revoked source, denied consent, missing handler and an external-app/browser return.
expected: Only deliberate permitted links reach the OS with the exact approved URL; native policy and bounds hold. Denial/missing handler return truthful errors and preserve owner/session authority.
evidence: Actual native handoff/return; external receiver exact URL; denied handoff counts and genuine SDK error.

testCases.title: Intent dispatch and channels
steps: Use two verified Routing Lab identities and a collision publisher. Query handlers, choose a target, exercise absent/ambiguous targets, first-open consent/decline and exact payload delivery.
Open symmetric INC channels; inject forged sender, foreign channel/request ID, replay, flood and malformed payloads; close/replace a target and change account during delayed delivery.
expected: Handler selection and payload follow verified target and selected contract; decline/cancel creates no target authority.
Sender/recipient/account/correlation are native-bound; stale/forged traffic fails closed without breaking a valid positive-control message.
evidence: Trusted handler review; genuine SDK payloads; target receiver counters; independent scope/correlation checks and late-delivery denials.

testCases.title: Notifications and configuration
steps: Register selected schemas; test valid/default/depth/type/secret values, Save/cancel/clear, invalid registration ACK + error push, incompatible update/removal and cold restart.

Use same app ID under another publisher/account and peer app; cancel account switching, then confirm switching and restore. Deliver delayed save/subscription/permission reads after revoke/close/update.
Request hostile and normal notifications in focused/unfocused views; test source/global concurrency limits, dismiss/action ownership, expiry with delayed permission reads, restart and grant revoke.
expected: Values/schema/grants are scoped and durable; masked secrets stay masked; invalid schema cannot overwrite values. Cancelled switch preserves registrations; actual change revokes them; removed schema purges orphaned values.

Notifications are attributed, bounded, dismissible shell UI; lifetime begins at admission, capacity rechecks after asynchronous permission, and actions cannot focus a foreign/replaced owner. No OS push claim.
evidence: Exact SDK ACK/error/value/subscription output; masked UI and cold read; identity/publisher cross-product; controlled-clock/native capacity and queued-revoke evidence.

testCases.title: Outbox destinations and receipts
steps: Using a protected disposable account, seed an exact signed kind-10002 list; publish one harmless primary through genuine Feed Lab SDK. Review full immutable primary/list union and exact signed list.
Test own-list fanout, explicit-only/toOutbox:false, duplicate required inboxes, all-required success and required rejected/unknown/cancelled target despite unrelated ACKs.
Test missing required inbox, union/frame overflow and ancillary-list failure. Independently observe each approved destination and verify exact primary/list events.
expected: One new primary signature and unchanged existing signed list go only to approved destinations. Primary/list receipts remain separate; ancillary failure preserves primary success.
Every required target must succeed; unrelated ACK cannot make primary successful. toOutbox:false omits own discovery/list only. Invalid required routing fails before review/sign/send.
evidence: Complete review/event hash; native signature/frame counts; controlled relay frames/receipts; independent exact signed stored-event readback. ACK and later storage remain separate.

testCases.title: Outbox frozen review, native faults and races
steps: Expire routing metadata and refresh before review; fail refresh; remove own list and inspect labelled Network fallback. Mutate routing/settings/metadata while review is pending.
Inject wrong source/domain/view/account/generation, foreign event/ACK ID, replay, late/concurrent callbacks and malformed payloads; retain a valid concurrent positive control.

Drive controlled accept/reject/AUTH/disconnect/accept-close/missing/foreign/malformed ACK, deadline, slow/flood/backpressure and primary/list/required partial fanout. Interrupt at review/sign/send/receipt with the T09 lifecycle variants.
expected: Review freezes exact targets/event; stale required refresh failure refuses publication; later settings do not alter approval.
Native owner binding, bounded slots/timers/frames and correlation fail closed. Unknown-after-send differs from cancelled-before-send; lifecycle revocation cannot revive old authority.
evidence: Ordinary app-UID/Expo/guest/protected signer composition; independent receiver exact frames and zero-emission proof where asserted; native zero-sign counters; race/timer/slot recovery; original failures retained.

testCases.title: Sandbox and capability failures
steps: Through malicious public-API fixtures send forged sibling/frame/main-frame messages, stale generation, malformed/oversized envelopes and ungranted operations.

Probe guest parent/native APIs, storage/secret access, fetch/XHR/WS/forms/images/navigation/popups/downloads and file/content URLs using a controlled receiver. Include independently observable DNS, UDP and public-HTTPS escape probes; local HTTP/TCP-only controls cannot establish all-origin egress denial.
Terminate/reload/navigate the content process and exhaust selected resource/session/queue limits. Inspect packaged bridge/manifest/service/URL registration for incoming signer-provider exposure.
expected: Only the trusted bundled host and exact verified native sender acquire scoped authority. Guests get no generic native bridge, secret, unrestricted network or signing/encryption API.
Failure tears down authority and stale callbacks; unsupported capability use returns honest denial. Phase 3 remains outgoing signer-client only; incoming signer services are absent.
evidence: Native adversarial checks and ordinary malicious guest results on each host; independent receiver escape counts; current package/bridge/service inspection; positive controls.
Reachable independent DNS/UDP/public-HTTPS receiver observations, with unrestricted positive controls, plus navigation/download/file/content probes and owning Expo/published composition.

testCases.title: Same-account signing methods and continuity
steps: Attach local and remote methods for the same npub; select one explicitly. Write State Lab data, change method, close/reopen and cold-launch. Keep another npub saved as a negative control.
Fail remote preflight, pre-dispatch and post-possible-dispatch while local remains attached. Then explicitly choose local and submit a fresh approved request.
Refresh relays and disconnect offline; cold-launch again, observing saved account/data, selected unavailable/no-method state and absence of pending replay.
expected: There is one account per npub; method changes preserve same-account data and do not select another account. No automatic fallback/retry occurs, even with local attached.
Explicit local selection can sign fresh work. Disconnect revokes remote credentials/authority but retains the account/data; restart preserves truthful no-method/unavailable state.
evidence: Public account/method snapshots and exact State values before/after restart; controlled signer/local counters; encrypted credential presence/absence and pending-operation count.

testCases.title: NIP-46 connection, correlation and browser Resume
steps: Connect a controlled signer through native Settings, confirm exact candidate public account, peer and selected normalized relay list; test decline, relay refresh and cold restart.

Exercise connection and signing authentication URLs: open the permitted browser, return without authenticating, then complete authentication and explicitly press native Resume. Test malformed/forbidden URL, cancel, background/lock and expiry.

Use wrong peer/author/request ID/account, invalid event hash/signature/content, duplicate/late encrypted reply, replay, response after relay change and exhausted original deadline. Repeat with a pinned independent real NIP-46 implementation.
expected: Credentials remain bounded/native-owned; authenticated peer/request/account correlation and exact signed event validation precede use. Browser return alone never releases a result.

Resume is explicit and revalidates original owner, generation, one-use ticket and absolute deadline. Repeated Resume/generation cannot extend time or resend. Possible signing dispatch plus later denial/expiry remains SIGNER_UNCERTAIN.
Controlled-peer tests and independent signer interoperability are reported separately; neither proves unrelated routes or physical protection.
evidence: Native Settings/review/Close/Resume input; controlled peer RPC/auth/sign counts and exact response verification; monotonic deadline ledger within one clock domain; independent real-signer version/ref.

testCases.title: All selected signing routes
steps: For local and NIP-46 on each host, approve one exact note, another supported update, Outbox primary + existing-list fanout and Blossom file authorization through ordinary app/public SDK paths.
On Android repeat all routes with NIP-55. For every route also reject/cancel and deliver a late response using T09; verify native file approval precedes signing for uploads.
expected: Every selected route uses the explicitly chosen method and identical exact native approval binding; returned event matches account, canonical hash, signature, kind, tags and content.

Independent destinations observe approved exact events/bytes only; unknown side effects remain unresolved until reconciled. UI/SDK completion, ACK, retrieval, new forwarding and controlled receiver consumption remain separate facts.
evidence: Route x platform x method ledger; full trusted review and SDK completion; native signature/dispatch counts; independent cryptography, relay/file receiver and readback.

testCases.title: Android NIP-55 and real signer
steps: On Android select the explicit signer package/certificate and candidate public account. Exercise public-key and exact event-sign requests with explicit external-app return and native Resume.

Test wrong/missing/changed package or certificate, absent handler, wrong Activity/result/request/account, cancellation, duplicate/late result, corrupted signature/hash and redundant result fields that do or do not match.
Repeat exact content/signature/publication and disconnect/cold restore with pinned real Amber; submit once and independently count each request/signature/publication.
expected: Only the explicitly bound provider and matching one-use Activity result can complete. Redundant fields are accepted only if exactly consistent. No silent signer substitution/local fallback occurs.
Possible provider dispatch followed by cancel/expiry/invalid result preserves uncertainty and original deadline. Exact-text or one-submit failures remain failed even if a valid event exists.
evidence: Android actual handoff/input and package/certificate binding; native controller/result counts; real-Amber version, canonical signed event/readback and exact content/count comparisons.
variants: Android only. iOS: not-applicable by platform contract, never counted as a passing NIP-55 test.

testCases.title: Fixture parity and whole-app published journey
steps: Build/verify UX, State, Approval, Feed, Resource, Upload and Routing fixture variants with genuine SDKs and stable visible identifiers; seal embedded/published byte hashes and signed publisher/version manifests.

From ordinary standalone Android/iOS run UX -> State -> Approval, then every capability case in this matrix through embedded and verified-published routes. Use disposable run accounts distinct from the release publisher, retained through restart.
Repeat a declared compatible third-party napplet sample, explicit update/restart and cross-account/publisher isolation. Reconcile each named requirement and retained failed result.
expected: The published product executes the exact reviewed fixture bytes after normal consent, without fixture signing/storage/approval bypass. A compatibility sample claims only exercised granted operations.

Both hosts complete each applicable group on final source-bound artifacts; shared/browser/simulator/packaging evidence alone never closes native final acceptance. Value/zaps and Value Lab are excluded.
evidence: Fixture/version/spec/source/artifact hashes; independent manifest/content retrieval; input and expected/actual records; every row-to-run mapping and unresolved gap.

testCases.title: Final quality, packages, notices and cleanup
steps: On the final candidate run the documented pinned checks and affected native suites; retain complete React Doctor and aislop reports. Inspect compatible dependency/protocol refs, locked patches and the complete actual delivered dependency/notice inventory.

Produce current locally signed standalone Android/iOS artifacts through documented native build/export instructions. Inspect identity/certificate, permissions, entitlements, backup/debug/network policy, packaged notices and runtime/source hashes.

Install/update without clearing retained data and cold-launch without Metro. Run final journeys; reconcile pending jobs/unknown side effects, remove only exact test-owned apps/runners/files, and verify retained app/data and before/after inventories. Record branch/status and preserve concurrent changes; source publication remains separately authorized.
expected: Both quality scores are 100/100 with findings fixed, no suppression/hidden advisories; incomplete/denied scans stay open. All applicable notices include required original license/NOTICE texts and match the delivered packages.
Build/signing/notice checks, physical security, ordinary runtime and full acceptance each have their own evidence. Build success is not acceptance.
Temporary ownership is exact; no test launcher/process remains and retained app data survives. No source remote/push mutation is inferred from acceptance work.
evidence: Complete quality/audit/compatibility reports; source/artifact seals; package/config/notice diff; no-Metro cold-launch input; exact cleanup and retained-account/data comparison.
